transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-27
Time: 10:00 PT (55 minutes)
Attendees: Ethan Rivera; Sofia Lin; Marcus O'Neill; Leah Kim; Jamie Patel; Ana Torres; + ~120 company listeners (stated)

[00:00:00] Ethan (Host): all right, hey everyone, thanks for joining the bridgeguard — um, bridgeguard crew signal. we'll go about 45, 50 minutes, keep it tight. Sofia, kick us off with the priorities?

[00:01:12] Sofia: yeah thanks Ethan. quick context — Q1 closed roughly on plan, but we saw a couple of margin surprises and the infra hiccup last week that bumped latency for a small set of tenants. so top-level for Q2: 1) stabilize infra and SLOs, 2) tighten cost/unit for hosted inference, 3) prioritize enterprise readiness for Dedicated and Private. i'll share a deck after this.

[00:02:45] Marcus: can i just interrupt — the incident, quick recap from infra side: it was a cascade starting with a bad kernel patch on a host group, KV cache thrash, then autoscaler reacted and we had a routing storm. not all requests failed but tail latency spiked. full incident timeline's on the doc, but the root causes are mixed infra + config.

[00:03:30] Ethan: and to be clear, customers saw errors and delays, some of our top accounts did ping CS, right? Jamie, were you on the triage?

[00:03:42] Jamie: yep, cs raised two tickets. we put in a temporary fallback to the older model variant and reduced batch size for some routes. that stopped the worst of it. want to note the KV cache says K V cash in the logs — uh, the telemetry naming made it messy to trace quickly.

[00:04:12] Leah: ok, two calls out of that: one, we need a better playbook for those routing storms — who toggles model fallback, who executes scaling policies. two, the kernel patch process needs a canary and a rollback step that's automated. i'm assigning engineering to own the playbook.

[00:05:00] Sofia: good. in terms of product tradeoffs — we have to decide whether to push aggressive batching back for hosted API to save cost but that increases observed latency for small requests. our thesis is cost-aware perf controls, but we can't surprise our customers mid-quarter.

[00:05:35] Marcus: i'm sympathetic. but also, some of the suggested optimizations are model-specific and require quantization variants for safe fallbacks. we need more bench coverage across sequence lengths. Leah, can we get a benchmarking sweep?

[00:06:05] Leah: yes, we'll schedule a sweep next week — but note resource contention; we might need dedicated pools to run exhaustive bench without impacting prod. that ties into budget asks.

[00:06:30] Ana (People Ops): hopping in on hiring — the reforecast reduces open headcount by ~8 roles for Q2, prioritizing infra, platform reliability, and SEs that support enterprise deals. i'll post the updated levels and role priorities.

[00:06:55] Sofia: that sounds reasonable. we need those SEs to support Dedicated pilots and Private deployments; pipeline suggests a few big deals could convert in Q2 if we show Private readiness.

[00:07:18] Ethan: quick question on runway math — finance, we trimmed non-essential spend as discussed, what's the new burn profile? (pause) okay I see an update in Confluence but can we get a short CFO note in the deck?

[00:08:00] Sofia: yes — i'll add a one-slide runway note.

[00:08:12] Marcus: returning to incident mitigations — proposed immediate actions: 1) stricter kernel rollouts with canary, 2) automated rollback on tail-latency thresholds, 3) centralize telemetry naming (KV cache vs KV-cache vs kv_cache) so triage is faster, 4) a control-plane guard that prevents rapid routing policy flips.

[00:09:05] Jamie: and from SE/support: we want an outbound template for affected customers. it needs to be specific — affected endpoints, mitigation done, and ETA for full postmortem.

[00:09:30] Ethan: agreed. i'll draft a template after today and Marcus will confirm technical details.

[00:10:00] (05:30 elapsed) Sofia: on product signals — a consistent ask: customers want clearer quantization and latency profiles per model variant. our optimize tool needs to generate suggested config for common app patterns. we're going to prioritize that as a cross-team ticket.

[00:11:20] Leah: re: Dedicated — ops asked for clearer autoscale contracts and burst rules. we need to bake those into the Dedicated onboarding so customers don't overprovision. Leah (laughs) sorry — that's me, but i'll own a template.

[00:12:10] Marcus: small note — some internal docs call the product Readwood Dedicated — tiny nit but it causes confusion in legal/ops. please standardize naming in the repo.

[00:12:35] Ethan: good catch. doc cleanliness is a low-effort win.

[00:13:00] (13:00 elapsed) Ana: quick people update — interviewing funnel is steady but slower at the senior levels. we'll shift a few onsite slots to virtual to speed up. also, manager calibration is next week.

[00:13:40] Sofia: any risks to SLAs or enterprise deals from the hiring slow down?

[00:13:52] Leah: maybe marginal for ramping SE support but not for baseline engineering. we should prioritize hiring for infra reliability and those SEs you mentioned.

[00:14:15] Jamie: question from chat — will there be more customer-facing benchmarks like the open model perf sheets? customers love that.

[00:14:28] Marcus: yes, that's in the product outreach plan. we'll publish model perf profiles for three common sequences next month.

[00:15:00] (15:00 elapsed) Ethan: ok let's do a rapid round: what do each of you want folks to remember from this call. Sofia?

[00:15:15] Sofia: stabilize infra, don't tinker with batching mid-quarter without comms, and i'll share Q2 priorities.

[00:15:28] Marcus: run the blackout drill, clean telemetry, and automate rollback.

[00:15:38] Leah: hire for reliability, benchmark across seq lengths, own the playbook for routing storms.

[00:15:50] Ana: hiring plan posted, interview velocity to increase via virtual on-sites.

[00:16:05] Jamie: craft customer comms and keep top-10 customers in the loop.

[00:16:20] (16:20 elapsed) (some cross-talk, a couple of attendees typing in chat)

[00:17:10] Ethan: moving to Q&A from the company — couple of questions came in via Slack. first: will pricing change because of the cost push?

[00:17:24] Sofia: short answer: no immediate pricing change. we'll run unit-cost optimizations and quantify impact; any pricing moves would be announced well in advance — we prefer configuring controls to preserve margins without surprising customers.

[00:18:05] Attendee (via chat): are we pausing new feature launches to focus on reliability?

[00:18:12] Leah: not a full pause — we'll gate launches that touch serving or routing and require an SRE sign-off. other product work continues.

[00:18:40] (18:40 elapsed) Marcus: note on Dedicated vs Private: for some regulated customers Private is the nonstarter unless we can show an on-prem package that meets their audit needs; legal and security are working on a checklist.

[00:19:05] Sofia: and that feeds into our sales plays — we need a 2-week readiness checklist for field. Ethan, partner channels want that too.

[00:19:22] Ethan: ok we'll produce a readiness checklist for sales and partners.

[00:19:40] (19:40 elapsed) Jamie: small but important point — our observability dashboards don't show token-level cost reasons well in the redwood console exports; SEs struggle to show customers per-route token economics.

[00:20:05] Leah: backlog item; we'll elevate to the console squad.

[00:20:30] (20:30 elapsed) Ana: hiring question from execs — we should finalize the list of roles that remain open and the pause list. i'll circulate a doc and we can sign off asynchronously.

[00:20:50] Sofia: good. next: comms cadence — we'll do a follow-up all-hands in 3 weeks focused on incident postmortem and bench results.

[00:21:10] Ethan: scheduling note: 3-week follow-up posted after this meeting.

[00:21:55] (21:55 elapsed) Public Q&A: someone asked about region coverage — APAC region capacity is improving but we still have spike risk during local business hours; ops is working with cloud partners on extra buffer.

[00:22:25] Marcus: yes, we're enabling autoscale policies per region as a short-term mitigation; long term we're looking at dedicated capacity in APAC regions.

[00:23:00] (23:00 elapsed) Sofia: a quick product demo note — the Optimize tool will get a new recommendation tab that suggests batching/quantization combos for a target latency. that'll be an internal alpha next month.

[00:24:30] Leah: remind engineering: no config flips in prod without a deploy window and a rollback play. that should be non-negotiable.

[00:25:10] (25:10 elapsed) Ethan: wrapping up — recap of commitments: Sofia will share the priorities deck and runway slide; Leah and Marcus deliver playbook items and bench schedule; Ana posts hiring plan; Ethan will coordinate customer comms.

[00:26:00] (final Q&A and misc applause in chat)

[00:26:30] Ethan: ok thanks all. meeting adjourned. next: follow-up all-hands in ~3 weeks to present postmortem and bench findings.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mislabels, some words slur or transcribe K V cash instead of KV cache. timestamps approximate.
